messages:
alex: Heads up — canary p95 spiked to ~420ms after the optimizer change. Not seeing user errors yet but telemetry shows kv-cache miss rate doubled for canary cohort. deploy-bot suggested an autorevert with medium confidence.

deploy-bot: ALERT: metric-threshold breach (p95 > 300ms). Suggested action: autorevert -> v2.6.1 (confidence=0.57). Possible causes: allocator tweak, kv-cache invalidation. Autorevert will run in 120s unless suppressed.

nina: suppress autorevert please. We need traces to rule out flakiness across hosts. If we revert now we lose span context.

oncall-jordan: agreed. Hold rollout and pin the canary route. Ops — can you capture a heap/trace snapshot?

ops-agent: starting: `rdwctl snapshot --scope canary --type traces,heap --since 10m --out s3://rdw-dumps/canary/1713479999-snap.tar.gz` 
ops-agent: snapshot complete and uploaded.

alex: pinned canary to v2.6.1: `releases pin --cohort canary --to v2.6.1 --reason "p95 spike; manual hold"` — pin applied. Posting a short customer notice to #customer-notices: "We paused a canary rollout for investigation; no customer impact observed."

nina: proposed rollback criteria: A) p95 <= 220ms for 15m after hotpatch OR B) error-rate delta > 0.4% -> rollback to v2.5.9. Also add: if flamegraphs show increased memcpy in allocator -> hotpatch revert first.

oncall-jordan: add: if autorevert is suppressed, log that in release notes and who suppressed it.

deploy-bot: NOTE: autorevert suppressed by user hold (actor: nina). To unsuppress: `deploybot enable-autorevert --actor auto`

ops-agent: analysis summary: flamegraphs indicate allocation path increased CPU and memcpy. Suspect experimental_alloc flag. Uploading details to #eng-runtime.

alex: ok, let's hotpatch-unset that flag first. Nina can you approve hotpatch?

nina: approve. Run: `opsctl patch kernelcfg --unset experimental_alloc --reason "canary perf regression"` then `rolling-restart --group canary --wait 45s`

ops-agent: applying hotpatch now...
ops-agent: ```
patch applied: experimental_alloc unset
restarting canary-01 ... ok
restarting canary-02 ... ok
restarting canary-03 ... ok
```

deploy-bot: MONITOR: p95 dropped 420ms -> 140ms within 4 minutes post-hotpatch. Autorevert still suppressed.

sam: great recovery. Recommendation: unpin and resume a cautious rollout, 10% -> 20% over 20m, and keep autorevert suppressed for 45m to avoid thrash.

alex: agreed. Sam, execute resume and update the release log. Also add a note to release notes: "Hotpatch revert applied to allocator flag; rollout resumed under monitoring."

sam: running resume: `releases resume --cohort canary --to v2.6.2 --increment 5%/5m --max 20%` 345: done. Posted update to #release-log and #customer-notices.

nina: assign postmortem owner: @nina, draft due EOD. Include timeline, decision rationale, and rollback criteria used.

oncall-jordan: I'll watch dashboards for the next 60m. If p95 crosses 300ms again, we escalate to full rollback plan: create ticket ops-RB-1713479999 and roll back to v2.5.9.

alex: thanks all. Closing this thread when postmortem link is posted.
